I have read the top post and all it seems to do is compare here to reddit. Users that use both sites please tell me the main differences that a casual user will notice.
Hello. Just arrived and am trying to get my head around what is going on here.
I think it's supposed to be very similar to reddit in functionality. The main difference is a commitment to non-censorship/protecting free speech, something reddit has lost.

I think the biggest difference is that everyone who's here now has a chance to influence changes since the site is only in alpha stage. On reddit, it can be months and sometimes years (if ever) before a heavily requested feature is implemented. Voat has the opportunity to build a stronger foundation than reddit's hack-job patchwork of code using the things that reddit doesn't do well as a guide.

One of the differences a casual user will notice first is the user page layout. It provides a bit more information and changes up the format to show submission distribution, voting habits, submission counters, and a breakdown of comment and post ratings. I like being able to see that information personally.

i second what this fine person is saying. Being on the ground level of a new site such as this with an emphasis on the user allows the user to learn from their experience on reddit and apply that knowledge here to make this a better more open discussion forum.
